stories.headline: Down Forty-Nine, and Still Four and Oh
stories.dek: The Machines trailed Lil' Chops 49-0 before they scored a point, and won it on the last throw of Sunday night. Nobody beats these people comfortably, including these people.
paragraphs: Here is a number for you: forty-nine to nothing. That was the state of this football game on Thursday night, by which I mean Aaron Rodgers threw three touchdown passes before The Machines had a man on the field. Quinshon Judkins ran one in. DK Metcalf caught a forty-three yarder. Lil' Chops put up half a hundred points before their opponents got out of bed, and I wrote a note to myself that said this one is finished.

I am an idiot. The Machines spent the rest of the weekend reeling it in a yard at a time — Derrick Henry, then Lamar Jackson twice, then Puka Nacua — and the whole thing came down to Jared Goff throwing eight yards on Sunday night with seven minutes left on our clock. That was the first time all game The Machines led. It was also the last lead change there was. 106.08 to 100.38.

What makes this worth writing down is that it is now a habit. The Machines are 4-0 and they have not won a comfortable game yet: 113-100 over the Powers of Pain, now this. Four weeks, 468 points, second in the league, and every single week they have been in a fight they could have lost. Either that is a team that knows how to finish or it is a team riding a coin that has come up heads four times. December will tell us which.

Lil' Chops fall to 2-2 and will not want to hear it, but Rodgers also threw two interceptions on that same Thursday night, and twenty-two points from a quarterback who hands back four is not the bargain it looks like. They also left Rashid Shaheed and his 11.3 on the bench for Garrett Wilson, who managed 2.7. In a game decided by 5.7. I am not going to say it. They know.

The Machines did the same thing, mind — Roman Wilson sat there with 13.4 while DJ Moore started and returned 1.7. Both of these managers got away with something. Only one of them got away with it twice.

stories.headline: A Kicker Beat Them, and They Helped
stories.dek: Jake Bates kicked three field goals on Sunday night to settle it for Master-Jeti. Killer Klowns had more than the margin sitting on their bench.
paragraphs: Killer Klowns led this game from Thursday night until Sunday night, which is most of it, and then a placekicker took it off them. Jake Bates hit from 54, then 43, then 41, and the middle one of those — Sunday night, with the whole thing level at 105 — was the moment it turned. Eighteen points from a man who does not play offence. That is the format for you.

Kenneth Walker had already done the heavy lifting for Master-Jeti, 29.9 of it, including a seventy-six yard run on Sunday afternoon that was the single best thing that happened in this match. Kyren Williams answered with 26.7 for the Klowns and two touchdowns inside four minutes, and for a while on Sunday morning this looked like a rout in the other direction. It was 91-33 at one point. It finished 118-105.

The part the Klowns will not enjoy: Keon Coleman scored 17.6 points on their bench while Marcus Mariota started and returned 4.4. That is a gap of 13.2 in a game they lost by 12.82. Not a near miss, not a what-if — the win was sitting right there in the drawer and nobody opened it.

Master-Jeti go to 3-1 and second in the Spartan. Killer Klowns go to 1-3, bottom of the same division, and have now lost three of four while scoring 365 points, which is not a disaster of a number. They are not being beaten. They are losing, which is different and worse.

stories.headline: The Best Bad Team in the League
stories.dek: BIG BLUE have scored more points than all but one team in the SCFL. They are 1-3. Beaver Eaters beat them and went four and oh.
paragraphs: Spencer Shrader kicked three field goals inside the first quarter and Beaver Eaters were 16-0 up before anybody on the other side had touched the ball, which sounds like the story and is not. BIG BLUE came back and led this game. Joe Burrow ran one in from a yard to put them in front at 81-78 just before halftime, CeeDee Lamb caught a twelve-yarder, and at the end of Sunday afternoon they were ahead by seven.

Then Bryce Young threw a thirty-two yard touchdown on Sunday night, Jahmyr Gibbs ran one in, Young threw another, and the game was gone in about ninety seconds of our clock. Javonte Williams finished with 26.3 and three touchdowns. Beaver Eaters are 4-0 and top of the entire league.

But the team I want to talk about is the losing one. BIG BLUE have scored 475 points in four weeks. Only Pork Chop Express have scored more, by a single point. They are averaging 119 a week, which would be good enough to beat most of this league most weeks. Their record is 1-3.

Look at how: beaten 112-90 in week one, beaten 112-111 in week three — one point, to the only other unbeaten side left — and now this. They have been handed the three highest-scoring opponents on the schedule so far and their reward is last-but-six in the table. If there is a more unlucky football team in this competition I have not found it, and I have been looking.
Beaver Eaters also left Drake Maye and his 26.8 on the bench and played Sam Darnold for 14.0. When you are 4-0 you get to call that a rotation decision.

stories.headline: Four Interceptions and a Long Walk Home
stories.dek: Wookie Leaks led this on Thursday night. By Monday they had been beaten by forty-one points, by a team that left twenty-one on the bench.
paragraphs: Harold Fannin caught a touchdown on Thursday night and Wookie Leaks led this football game for most of two days. Then Jacoby Brissett threw three interceptions, Jalon Daniels threw two of his own in reply, and what had been a contest turned into whichever quarterback could stop giving it away first. Daniels stopped. Brissett did not.

The lead changed once, on Sunday afternoon, when Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught twenty-eight yards to put Pork Chop Express in front at 43.26. Nobody went near it after that. Matt Gay kicked three field goals, Brock Bowers scored, Chris Olave caught a forty-four yarder on Monday night when it had long stopped mattering, and it finished 100.22 to 58.62.

Now the detail that ought to frighten the rest of this division. Pork Chop Express won by 41.6 points with Kyle Monangai sitting on their bench scoring 27.0, while D'Andre Swift started and returned 5.4. They were twenty-one and a half points worse than they could have been and it was still the second-biggest beating of the week.

They are 3-1 and have 476 points, the most in the league. Wookie Leaks are 1-3 with 300, which is the second-fewest, and they have now been beaten by 55, by 27 and by 42. Their one win was against a side that has lost four straight. That is not a slump, that is the table telling the truth.

stories.headline: Bijan Robinson Arrived Too Late
stories.dek: The Powers of Pain took the lead in the first quarter and never gave it up. Smoke Dragons concede more than anybody, and it is catching up with them.
paragraphs: Nico Collins caught forty-five yards on Sunday morning, put the Powers of Pain in front, and that was the game. Not the best play, not the biggest — the last lead change there was, with three-quarters of the weekend still to come. They led by thirty-six at one point. C.J. Stroud threw two touchdowns to Collins, Brock Purdy threw one of fifty-six yards on Sunday afternoon, Sam LaPorta scored on Sunday night, and all Smoke Dragons could do was keep pace badly.

Jameis Winston was busy — three touchdown passes, 19.0 points, two interceptions to go with them, which is the Winston experience in a sentence. Malachi Fields caught a touchdown and added a forty-yarder. It was not enough and it was never going to be.

Then Monday night, and Bijan Robinson ran fifty-nine yards for a touchdown, and four yards for another one, and finished the week with 26.7 — the best number on either roster. By the time the first of those went in his team were thirty-four points behind. There is a particular cruelty in a man playing that well on a Monday in a game that ended on Sunday.

Smoke Dragons drop to 2-2 and the worry is not the record, it is the other column: 408 points conceded in four weeks, the second-worst in the league, and 320 scored, which is fourth-worst. They have been beaten 120-44 and now 136-101. The two wins were by 19 and by 3. This is a team winning narrowly and losing enormously, and over fourteen weeks that arithmetic does not end anywhere good.

One more, and it is a sore one: Brian Robinson scored 24.7 on their bench while Jaylen Warren started in the same slot for 12.6. Twelve points. They lost by thirty-five, so it changes nothing, which is the only reason to mention it at all.

stories.headline: StillTheCream Win One, Finally, In About an Hour
stories.dek: Ten lead changes before one o'clock on Sunday, then one enormous hour, and a first win of the season. Guido Haters had the answer on their bench.
paragraphs: Ten lead changes in this football game and every single one of them happened before one o'clock on Sunday. Deshaun Watson and Denzel Boston spent Thursday night trading the thing back and forth like a hot plate — six changes of lead in the first quarter alone, which I have not seen before and would rather not see again, because I had to write each one down.

Then, at 14-13, somebody turned the lights on. Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked from 51. Jordan Love threw a touchdown. Rhamondre Stevenson ran one in. Fairbairn kicked from 54. George Pickens caught fifty-three yards, Love threw another, Tucker Kraft scored. In the space of one Sunday-morning hour StillTheCream went from 14 points to 85 and the game simply stopped being competitive.

It is their first win of the year, which matters more than the manner of it. They came in 0-3 having scored 178 points in three games — the worst offence in the league by a distance — and they have now put up 96.9 in a single afternoon. One week does not undo three. It does suggest the roster is not as empty as the table said it was.

Guido Haters had their own hour late on, Emanuel Wilson scoring twice and Kirk Cousins throwing two more, and they closed to within fifteen. They also started Ja'Marr Chase for 2.7 while Romeo Doubs scored 17.8 on the bench. Fifteen points of difference in a nineteen-point defeat. It would not quite have won it. It would have made the last hour interesting, which is more than most managers get.

stories.headline: Two Men, Two Nights, One Game
stories.dek: Chuba Hubbard spent Sunday night dragging Phins Phag into the lead on his own. On Monday, Alvin Kamara did exactly the same thing back.
paragraphs: Ten lead changes, two teams who could not shake each other off for three days, and in the end it came down to two running backs who were never on the field together and never will be.

Through Sunday afternoon this was n.W.o's. Patrick Mahomes threw two touchdowns, Will Reichard kicked from 47, 50, 41 and 29 — a placekicker, outscoring every skill player his manager owns, 19.0 of them — and they led 68-51 going into the evening with the thing apparently settled.

Then Chuba Hubbard played Sunday night. Not his team: him. Twenty-one carries' worth of it, two touchdowns, 24.9 points, every single one of them after seven o'clock, and when he went in from two yards at the end of it Phins Phag led 70.94 to 69.46 for the first time since the second quarter. n.W.o had nothing left on the field. Everybody they owned had already played.

Except one. Alvin Kamara took Monday night and did the identical thing in reverse — three yards for a touchdown to take the lead back at 4:15 on our clock, five yards for another with forty-five seconds to go, 17.8 points, all of them after the rest of the league had gone to bed. 85.26 to 76.34.

n.W.o are 2-2 and thoroughly average in a way that four weeks has not resolved: 340 points scored, 364 conceded, two wins, two defeats, nothing to tell you which it is. Phins Phag are 0-4 and last in the league, and the hard part is that they played well here. Hubbard was the best man on the field by six points. They still lost. That is what 0-4 feels like from the inside, and there are ten weeks of it left to get out of.

stories.headline: Gumbas Spent the Second Quarter Below Zero
stories.dek: Horsecollars won by 59 and are unbeaten. Three weeks ago they won by one. Nothing about this team's record describes how it was earned.
paragraphs: There is not a great deal to report here and I am going to report it anyway, because the numbers are genuinely remarkable. Gumbas were on minus 1.86 points partway through the second quarter. Not a low score. A negative one. Matthew Stafford threw two interceptions and that, for a while, was the sum total of the contribution.

By then Jonathan Taylor had run in two touchdowns, Zay Flowers had caught one and added a fifty-two yarder, Brandon Aubrey had kicked a fifty, and Geno Smith had thrown a fifty-eight yard touchdown. It was 69.58 to 0.54. The game was over before anybody had their coat off.

To their credit Gumbas did eventually arrive. Tyquan Thornton caught two touchdowns and two long balls for 23.1, George Kittle caught a fifty-six yard touchdown on Sunday afternoon worth 11.6 — the single biggest play anyone made all week, in a game that had been decided for two hours. Tetairoa McMillan then scored twice more on Sunday night for 31.2 just to settle the argument.

Horsecollars are 4-0 and third in the league, and here is the thing worth noticing about them: three weeks ago they beat BIG BLUE 112-111. One point. This week they won by 59.46. Same team, same month. They have a 456-point offence and no identity yet, and until somebody beats them we have no idea whether they are the best team in this league or the luckiest.
Gumbas fall to 1-3 with 294 points, the fewest of anybody, and have now been beaten by 41, by 44 and by 59. The one week they won, they scored 79. This is not a form problem.
